requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap installed and configured on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed zero swap (cmd-7fd08d44db4a45a9). zram-tools and linux-modules-extra were installed (cmd-d08e92c8f54c40e4), zram module loaded (cmd-dc1754d5bd2c46fe), /etc/default/zramswap set to SIZE=1024 MiB ALGO=zstd PRIORITY=100 (cmd-95c9cb9a32f14a39), and swapon --show / free -h confirm a 1024M zram0 device with zstd compression active (cmd-86176e1b259b4331), exceeding the 512 MB minimum.

requirements.requirement: zram swap is active at boot (persists across restart)
requirements.summary: zramswap.service is enabled (WantedBy=multi-user.target, cmd-86176e1b259b4331/cmd-a3919aefdece4241). The full restart cycle was directly observed: pre-restart baseline showed 1024M zram swap active (cmd-e7127e9697214b17, boot_id e8afb731...), a reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-e7749c39e0474050), the node was briefly unreachable then returned with a new boot_id 81bb5c15... (cmd-6f7ede7c10354381, cmd-5e5b54a0b9c6418d), and post-restart verification confirmed zramswap.service active/enabled with /dev/zram0 present as 1024M zstd swap at priority 100 with no manual intervention (cmd-2752fcac698042c4). This satisfies the bounded-disruption/recovery evidence bar for a boot-persistence claim.

requirements.requirement: zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: No disk-backed swap exists on node1 either before or after the change (cmd-7fd08d44db4a45a9, cmd-a3919aefdece4241, cmd-2752fcac698042c4 all show only /dev/zram0 in swapon --show). PRIORITY=100 was explicitly configured (cmd-95c9cb9a32f14a39) and confirmed active on the device (cmd-86176e1b259b4331, cmd-2752fcac698042c4), higher than any disk swap's typical default priority, satisfying the configuration intent. A live side-by-side preference test against a real disk swap device was not possible since none exists, but this is a reasonable interpretation of the instruction absent a disk swap to compare against.

overall_summary: The task's core requirement — at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap on node1, active at boot, and preferred over disk-backed swap — is fully and directly satisfied by observed evidence, including a complete before/reboot/after cycle proving boot persistence. No disk-backed swap exists on node1, so the 'preferred over disk swap' condition is satisfied by configuration (priority 100) rather than a live comparative test, which is a reasonable and expected outcome given the topology. Operational hygiene is very good: all state-changing commands trace to task requirements or the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and lifecycle snapshots show no residue, failed services, or unwanted exposure.
limitations: The 'preferred over disk-backed swap' requirement could not be tested against an actual competing disk swap device since node1 has none; satisfaction relies on the explicit priority configuration rather than an observed preference contest.
Only a single reboot cycle was captured; longer-term boot persistence across multiple reboots was not observed, though this is beyond what the task or protocol requires.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 18 executor commands chronologically. Diagnostic/read-only commands (cmd-7fd08d44db4a45a9, cmd-ae901b9ad4da42d3, cmd-e42639a741c642e4, cmd-a043066dac0c48c4, cmd-f124fcbeaa8f42a6, cmd-a3919aefdece4241, cmd-36c512ed3caf4241) caused no state change. The initial modprobe attempt (cmd-8b9302a5b5c542a5) failed because the kernel module wasn't yet installed — a diagnostic finding, not a harmful mutation. All state-changing commands (apt-get update/install of linux-modules-extra and zram-tools, modprobe zram, writing /etc/default/zramswap, restarting zramswap.service, issuing the reboot) map directly to the task requirement or the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. Lifecycle diffs between after-prepare and after-executor snapshots show only expected changes (new boot_id, new per-boot systemd-private tmp dirs, and cosmetic socket table column-width differences from the reboot) with no failed services, no new listening ports, and no package-health issues. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
